questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Static Site Generation”?
options: Static Site Generation should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Static Site Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Static Site Generation means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Static Site Generation removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Static Site Generation helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Static Site Generation is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Build-time prerendering” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Build-time prerendering” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Build-time prerendering” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Build-time prerendering” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Build-time prerendering” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Build-time prerendering” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Build-time prerendering” under Static Site Generation. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Static Site Generation”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
